## 1. Identification Strategy  
Regression Discontinuity (RD) design exploiting the deterministic “round–to–nearest-integer’’ rule that maps the continuous minority‐population share into a discrete number of reserved seats.

Why it fits  
• Treatment intensity (number of seats) jumps discretely at known, exogenous population-share thresholds that are almost infinitesimal (0.5-percentage-point multiples of the seat-share).  
• States just below and just above a threshold are plausibly identical except for receiving one extra reserved seat, satisfying the local‐randomization intuition behind RD.  
• We observe many independent cut-offs (one for every integer seat count × three Censuses), giving ample power and allowing pooling with “stacked’’ RD.

Type of RD  
Sharp RD for the mapping minority share → number of reserved seats (first stage).  
Reduced-form RD for policy outcomes; or 2SLS (RD-IV) with “extra reserved seat’’ as instrument for actual SC/ST seat share.

## 2. Treatment and Control  

Treatment variable  
T_{st} = 1{ state s in year t received *one more* reserved seat because the census-based expected seat share crossed a 0.5 threshold }.  
For intensity analyses: ΔSeats_{st} = actual_reserved_seats – floor(expected_seats).

Control group  
States whose minority share places them just below the same threshold (they receive the lower number of reserved seats).

Timing / variation  
Key shocks occur when a new Census is implemented (1961, 1971, 1981) and retained until the next delimitation. We align outcomes to the post-census electoral terms; pre-census outcomes can be used as falsification tests.

## 3. Key Identifying Assumptions  

A1. Continuity of potential outcomes in minority share at the cut-off.  
Plausible: population shares are predetermined and not manipulable by states; nothing else changes discontinuously at exactly 0.5 rounding points.

A2. No strategic manipulation of the running variable.  
Highly plausible—the Census is conducted by the national statistical office; states cannot finely tailor SC/ST counts to hit/not hit thresholds.

A3. Local Stable Unit Treatment Value (no spillovers across states within the chosen bandwidth).  
Reasonable given state autonomy over most redistributive programs; we can cluster by state‐year and check robustness excluding spatial neighbors.

A4. Correct functional form / bandwidth choice.  
We will implement data-driven MSE-optimal bandwidths and robust bias-corrected confidence intervals (Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik, 2014).

A5. Implementation of the rule.  
Historical evidence shows the Election Commission applied the rounding rule mechanically in all 16 major states for every delimitation between 1960-92.

## 4. Threats to Identification & Remedies  

1. Census mis-measurement of minority population  
  Remedy: show that pre-treatment covariates and lagged outcomes are smooth at the threshold; repeat RD using alternative sources (National Sample Survey) as running variable.

2. Other institutional changes coinciding with new Census cycles  
  Remedy: include Census-cycle fixed effects; run donut RD omitting ±1 year around the census announcement; placebo thresholds at ±0.25 levels.

3. Serial correlation / mean reversion in state policies  
  Remedy: use state and year fixed effects in a panel RD (difference-in-discontinuities); cluster standard errors at the state level; run leads–lags event-study to show parallel pre-trends.

## 5. R Code Outline  

```r
# 0. Packages --------------------------------------------------------------
library(tidyverse)
library(lfe)             # for high-dim panel regressions
library(rdrobust)        # Calonico-Cattaneo-Titiunik RD

# 1. Load data -------------------------------------------------------------
dat <- read_csv("india_state_RD_1960_92.csv")

# 2. Construct running variable and treatment -----------------------------
dat <- dat %>%
  mutate(expected_seats = total_seats * scst_share,          # continuous
         floor_seats     = floor(expected_seats),
         frac_part       = expected_seats - floor_seats,
         # rounding threshold at 0.5
         treat           = if_else(frac_part >= 0.5, 1, 0),
         running         = frac_part - 0.5)                  # 0 at cutoff

# Keep observations within a symmetric bandwidth of +/-0.25 seat share
dat_rd <- dat %>% filter(abs(running) <= 0.25)

# 3. Main RD regression (reduced form) -----------------------------
# Robust bias-corrected local linear RD
rd_res <- rdrobust(
  y  = dat_rd$scst_welfare_spend_pc,   # example outcome
  x  = dat_rd$running,
  c  = 0,
  covs = dat_rd %>% select(gdp_pc, urban_rate, party_left_dummy) %>% as.matrix()
)
summary(rd_res)

# 4. 2SLS RD (instrumenting actual seat share) ---------------------
# First stage
fs <- rdrobust(y = dat_rd$scst_mla_share, x = dat_rd$running, c = 0)
# Second stage
dat_rd <- dat_rd %>%
  mutate(fitted_mla_share = fs$Yhat)
iv_mod <- felm(scst_welfare_spend_pc ~ fitted_mla_share |
               0 | 0 | state, data = dat_rd)
summary(iv_mod)

# 5. Robustness check: donut RD (drop +/- 0.02 around cut-off) ----
dat_donut <- dat_rd %>% filter(abs(running) > 0.02)
rd_donut  <- rdrobust(y = dat_donut$scst_welfare_spend_pc,
                      x = dat_donut$running, c = 0)
summary(rd_donut)
```

## 6. Expected Results  

Direction: Positive. One additional reserved seat (≈0.7 percentage-point rise in SC/ST legislative share for the median state) should increase per-capita spending on minority welfare, raise SC/ST public-sector employment, and accelerate land reform implementation.

Magnitude (back-of-the-envelope):  
• Welfare spending: +2–3 % of the existing SC/ST welfare budget per extra seat (≈0.05 % of state expenditure).  
• Minority public-sector share: +0.3 pp.  
These priors stem from median elasticity of budget allocations to vote share found in other contexts (≈0.2–0.3).

## 7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (1 = good, 0 = bad)

1. Running variable observes no manipulation …… 1  
2. Covariate balance near cut-off ………………… 0.9 (will test)  
3. Large, precise first stage (ΔReservedSeats→ΔMLAshare) … 1  
4. Adequate observations within optimal bandwidth ………… 0.8  
5. Robustness across bandwidths & specifications ………… 0.9  

Overall: high internal validity conditional on passing balance and placebo tests.
